findings.title: Patch interception does not enforce the no-patching rule
findings.description: D7 claims wrapping `_patch` covers `patch.dict`, but `patch.dict` uses the separate `_patch_dict` implementation. Additionally, a project module’s namespace dictionary is not itself a project module, class or instance, so the stated owner check does not reject it. Tests could patch project code and still qualify, violating the architecture’s mandatory fairness rule. Cover dictionary patching explicitly, including project-namespace ownership.

findings.title: Hidden-test dependencies have no injection contract
findings.description: Closure digests recognize test-side helpers and constants, but the case handoff contains only test node ids and added `conftest.py` fixtures. A new hidden test can qualify using an added helper because qualification overlays whole files; 425’s test-level injection has no specified way to preserve that helper. Define how required support definitions reach grading, or reject unsupported dependencies. Otherwise a qualified reference need not pass when graded.

findings.title: Re-qualification can validate a different immutable case
findings.description: Re-qualification may change hidden or excluded tests, which changes the case id under 421 D1. However, `qualification_for(case, environment)` checks environment and rule version without explicitly requiring the returned record’s `case_id` to match the requested case. Specify that changed-content qualification cannot validate the old case-set entry; it must be dropped or introduced through a new versioned case set.

findings.title: Yield aggregation can count the same candidate multiple times
findings.description: D10 retains records per environment, including pre-sandbox records, while D12 aggregates qualification records without a selection rule. One commit can therefore contribute multiple qualifications or conflicting outcomes, inflating the case count used for separability. Define one eligible outcome per candidate for each report, with explicit environment and rule-version selection.

findings.title: The separability answer is not supported by the paired statistic
findings.description: The proposed variance bound assumes constant true differences across cases and independent samples. The document acknowledges that case heterogeneity invalidates its “enough cases” conclusion, yet that conclusion determines initiative ordering. The architecture and slice plan require an answer under the paired per-case statistic. Report this calculation as a conditional planning estimate, not established sufficiency, or use a conservative bound that accounts for heterogeneous paired differences.

findings.title: New subprocess and network paths lack explicit failure contracts
findings.description: Generic `harness_error` handling does not define execution bounds and malformed/partial-output handling for the new issue fetch, collection, boundary resolver and trace calls. Resolver failure is also classified inconsistently: D6 specifies rejection, while the technical requirements expect `harness_error` for a resolver crash. Specify inherited or new timeouts, child termination, handling of interrupted responses, and consistent candidate outcomes. These paths must not hang or turn incomplete evidence into qualification.

structured_findings.summary: Patch interception does not enforce the no-patching rule
Hidden-test dependencies have no injection contract
Re-qualification can validate a different immutable case
Yield aggregation can count the same candidate multiple times
The separability answer is not supported by the paired statistic
New subprocess and network paths lack explicit failure contracts
